The perception of American cues increases aggressive constructs and judgments of other people in memory for American news watchers, but not for non-news watchers.

(a) nonconscious perceptions of American cues increase aggression in Americans who regularly watch American news; (b) these effects do not occur in Americans who do not watch American news; and (c) the effects are not moderated by participants' political party affiliation.
